A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same human-versus-automatic AI-text detection study. Their text, tables, figures, and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original human detection experiments on 300 articles, a fiction pilot in Appendix C, and automatic and prompt-based detector evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the main detector comparison in Table 2, fiction results in Table 16, and supplementary detector results in Table 23.

M1.justification: The expert-derived humanization procedure, explanation coding, and zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and guide-based detectors are retained. Corresponding prompts match after renumbering; relocated descriptions do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both use the same nonfiction corpus from eight publications, five generation/evasion conditions, and r/WritingPrompts fiction pilot. Newly cited multilingual research and discussion of commercial humanizers do not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The same Pangram variants, GPTZero, Binoculars variants, Fast-DetectGPT, and RADAR comparisons remain. The appendices also retain e5-lora and the same additional LLM detector comparisons.

E3.justification: The paired 30-human/30-AI article batches, expert screening, randomized within-subject design, TPR/FPR metrics, and 40-article threshold calibration remain unchanged. V2 justifies the existing five-expert sample without reporting a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: The same prompting ablations, paraphrasing and humanization tests, humanizer-development trials, and individual-expert/error analyses remain. Appendix D.3 and Figure 9 reorganize existing analyses rather than introduce new ones.

E5.justification: Both retain the same descriptive statistics and annotator confidence ratings. V2 introduces no repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or revised statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Main results in v1 Table 3/v2 Table 2, fiction results in Table 16, and supplementary results in v1 Table 22/v2 Table 23 match. Clue frequencies and plotted data are also retained; changes such as 80 to 80.0 and 4.027 to 4.03 are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical results or proofs. The empirical metric definitions remain unchanged, with no substantive mathematical additions or revisions.

C1.justification: V2's introduction newly asserts that nonexperts overestimate their detection ability. The central claims about expert-majority accuracy, robustness, explanatory capabilities, and human-inspired detection remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit discussion of small-sample generalization and frames expert selection as investigating an upper bound on human performance (Section 2 and Appendix A.1). It also interprets nonexpert confidence as overconfidence and expands discussion of high-stakes human review versus its limited scalability (Section 3).

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies an MIT license for released annotations and reports a cost of $865 per annotator across five experiments. Recruitment thresholds, prompts, model settings, detector thresholds, and the repository link were already present and are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lipton (2018) on interpretability and Wang et al. (2025) on multilingual human detection. It prunes references including Jakesch (2023), Brooks (2024), Kobak (2024), and sentence-level detection work, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 1-5 undergo extensive condensation and rewriting, with generation examples, detector descriptions, and commentary shifted into reorganized appendices. V2 removes a duplicated paragraph from Table 14 but also introduces unfinished prose and an empty Appendix D.2.

P2.justification: V1's full taxonomy becomes an abridged main Table 3 plus full appendix Table 17. Its two-panel Figure 3 is split between v2 Figures 3 and 9, the article-length table moves to the appendix, and appendix figures and prompt tables are extensively repacked.

improvement.justification: V2's added sample-size qualifications, discussion of appropriate uses of human review, and explicit annotation license modestly improve transparency and usefulness while preserving the experimental evidence. Editorial defects, including empty Appendix D.2 and a stale Figure 3 reference for false positives, limit the gain.
